sections.h2: What can the Bay County Register of Deeds office do for a seller?
sections.html:
Think of this office as the county's land filing cabinet. It takes in deeds, mortgages, lis pendens notices and certified copies, indexes each one, and holds the public record that every title company reads before a Bay County closing.

The counter keeps weekday hours of 8:00 a.m. through 5:00 p.m. Staff research time ends half an hour earlier, at 4:30, and the office does not close for lunch. Beginning January 1, 2018, each instrument receives a single Document Number in place of the old Liber and Page pair.

  • Doxpop offers search any hour of the day. Its help line, 1-866-369-7671, assists with account sign up.
  • Doxpop Property Watch emails you free of charge whenever someone attempts to transfer title to your land.
  • Approved eRecording partners are listed on the office page for electronic delivery.
  • Anything sent through USPS, UPS or FedEx should come with a self addressed stamped envelope for the return trip.

sections.h2: What will recording a deed in Bay County set me back?
sections.html:
Bay County's statutory fee schedule sets one flat charge: $30.00 per document, covering deeds, mortgages, lis pendens notices and similar instruments. Four of those dollars are passed to the Michigan State Survey and Remonumentation fund. Fixture filings, state and federal liens, state deeds, plats and tax reversion papers skip the $4.00 share.

Charges at the Bay County Register of Deeds. Source: Bay County Register of Deeds recording fee page.

County transfer tax$1.10 per $1,000 of price

MCL 211.135 drives the certificate: it applies to deeds carrying a warranty clause, land contracts, warranty assignments of land contracts and condominium master deeds.

sections.h2: Why might Bay County reject my deed?
sections.html:
The office posts sixteen rules drawn from Michigan recording statutes. A paper that misses one comes back unrecorded, and a delay of several days can derail a closing date. The flaws below are the ones sellers meet most.

  • Ink signatures must be originals. The signer's name is printed under the line, and it has to match the notary's certificate word for word.
  • Deeds must list the grantee's mailing or street address, along with the preparer's name and address.
  • Someone with Michigan authority, such as a notary, judge or court clerk, must acknowledge any paper that conveys or burdens land.
  • Leave 2.5 inches blank at the top of page one and half an inch around every other edge, using black type of 10 point or larger on white stock.
  • Sheets must measure between 8.5 by 11 and 8.5 by 14 inches, and line one must announce what the instrument is.
  • A deed that mentions a survivor has to be paired with a certified death certificate, either attached or already of record.
  • Court orders need the clerk's certification and seal, and Social Security numbers must lose their first five digits.

Another rule on the list requires conveyances to state the marital status of male grantors, tied to MCLA 565.221.

sections.h2: How is transfer tax calculated on a sale in Bay County?
sections.html:
Recording triggers two levies: a county tax under MCL 207.505 and a state tax under MCL 207.526. The deed must show the whole price on its face, or the filer must present a Real Estate Transfer Affidavit stating it. Both taxes apply unless an exemption fits, and the document itself must claim that exemption.

Run the numbers for a house priced at the Census median of $152,200. The state share at $7.50 per thousand is roughly $1,141, the county share at $1.10 per thousand is roughly $167, and about $1,309 is collected when the deed is recorded.

The two exemption lists overlap but are not identical. Each excludes consideration below $100, security instruments, leases, court orders that set no price, land contracts under which title has not yet passed, and foreclosure transfers involving government backed loans. Only the state act also names transfers from a parent or grandparent to a child or grandchild. Ask the title agent or the office which section covers your paper.

sections.h2: Which state fee rules stand behind the Bay County schedule?
sections.html:
MCL 600.2567, part of the Revised Judicature Act, caps what a register of deeds may collect, and the Bay County page cites it by name. The statute also prices the services that sellers and heirs request most often.

  • A photocopy of a record is $1.00 a page, and a certification stamp on a recorded paper is $5.00.
  • A search of grantor and grantee indexes is 50 cents for each year searched, with a floor of $5.00.
  • Filing and noting some other paper is $1.00.
  • Payment arrives when the paper is left for recording, except for electronic filings and government filers who hold a payment agreement.

Charter counties may adopt their own schedule by ordinance, so verify any copy or search charge with Bay County staff before mailing a check.

sections.h2: In what order should a seller handle recording in Bay County?
sections.html:
Work in this order and you save a trip. Settle who must sign and whether a survivor appears on the deed, so the death certificate is on hand. Request the tax certificate from the County Treasurer if the deed has a warranty clause. Have the deed drafted with the full price written in, or complete the transfer affidavit. Then notarize it in Michigan and give the original to the title agent, or mail it with a return envelope.

Once the paper is recorded, you receive a Document Number, which is how the instrument turns up in the online index. Keep it with your closing file. Anyone who holds other land in the county should also enroll in Property Watch.

When a paper bounces, the cause usually sits on the sixteen item list: a name that does not match, a narrow margin, an unsealed court order or an exposed Social Security number. Correct that single defect and resubmit instead of redrafting everything.

sections.h2: How does the Register of Deeds connect with other Bay County offices?
sections.html:
A sale involves several counters. The Treasurer, upstairs in the county building at 515 Center Ave., writes the tax certificate and collects late tax. Equalization answers parcel and description questions. The assessor in your city or township keeps the value record, while the Register preserves the chain of title.

The county lies along Saginaw Bay on the east side of Michigan's Lower Peninsula, with 14 townships and 4 cities. Census QuickFacts for 2020 to 2024 gives the middle owner occupied home a value of $152,200, owner occupancy of 77.0 percent, 45,103 households and median household income of $61,763. New construction is slight: 67 building permits were counted for 2025.

faqs.q: How much does Bay County charge to record a document?
faqs.a: A flat $30.00 for each document, and $4.00 of that goes to the state survey and remonumentation fund. A paper that assigns or discharges multiple instruments adds $3.00 for every extra one.

faqs.q: Are Bay County land records searchable on the web?
faqs.a: They are. Doxpop runs a search service around the clock, and the office suggests enrolling in its free Property Watch alert to learn of any attempt to move your title.

faqs.q: Is eRecording available in Bay County?
faqs.a: It is. The office page names the approved partners that deliver title documents electronically to the county.

faqs.q: What does the Bay County tax certificate cost on a warranty deed?
faqs.a: Five dollars, paid on a check that is separate from the recording fee and made out to the Bay County Treasurer instead of the Register of Deeds.

faqs.q: What transfer tax rates does Bay County list?
faqs.a: The Register shows $7.50 per $1,000 of consideration for the state and $1.10 per $1,000 for the county. An exempt transfer must say why on the instrument.
